subject: Capture classification and non-training assurance for HealthCore data
messages:
From: Susan Liu <susan.liu@healthcore.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@healthcore.com
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2028 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Capture classification and non-training assurance

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking our call yesterday. HealthCore is preparing a DPA addendum to cover our pilot and we need to confirm a few operational commitments before legal will sign:

- A clear no-model-training / no-improvement commitment for customer-provided content (we need language that covers interactive prompts and uploaded files).
- Confirmation of who retains ownership of prompts and generated responses (HealthCore needs to keep derivative/output rights).
- Evidence we can evaluate: runbook or artifacts that show telemetry is not used for model updates, list of subprocessors (and which are onshore), and an architectural diagram showing where data may be cached or logged.
- Residency options or KMS region guarantees for onshore key material.

Can you confirm whether Redwood offers an account-level switch to disable model improvement, and whether you can produce an "evidence pack" (logs, config flags, subprocessor list) that our security team can consume? Also please indicate typical turnaround for an evidence request and whether any of the subprocessors process raw prompts.

We're aiming to finalize the addendum by the end of next week (7/6). If you can send a short checklist and an ops contact who will provide the evidence, that would help.

Appreciate it,

Susan Liu
Senior Counsel, HealthCore
susan.liu@healthcore.com

--
Attachment: HCor_DPA_Redline_v0.1.docx (see referenced redline in body)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Susan Liu <susan.liu@healthcore.com>
Cc: david.kim@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capture classification and non-training assurance

Hi Susan — thanks for the clear list. Looping in David (privacy) and Jonas (infrastructure) to provide the ops/evidence detail. High level answers below, then David/Jonas can add specifics: 

- No-training toggle: Yes — we support an account-level "model_improvement=false" configuration for Hosted and Dedicated customers. When enabled, customer interaction data is not routed to any training pipelines and is treated as operational telemetry only (retained for a short window for debugging and then purged per retention policy).

- Ownership: Redwood's standard position in the DPA is that customers retain ownership of inputs and outputs; we only reserve operational rights necessary to provide the service (metrics, telemetry). We are happy to include explicit derivative/output language in the addendum to match HealthCore's requirements.

- Evidence pack: We can produce a limited-scope evidence pack that includes: subprocessor inventory (with processing purpose), a short ops architecture diagram, audit-log samples (redacted), and the config flag values for your tenant. Typical turnaround for an initial pack is 2–4 business days; full forensic exports can take longer.

- Subprocessors & onshore options: We'll include the current subprocessor list; for Dedicated/private deployments we can discuss onshore lane options for certain subprocessors (and customer-managed KMS).

Next steps I'd propose: 1) I will share a short checklist and confirm the expected deliverables by EOD; 2) David/Jonas will confirm technical artifacts and estimated delivery; 3) we'll provide the evidence pack within 72 business hours after you sign an NDA/addendum that covers the export. Does that timeline work?

Thanks — Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Head of Customer Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2028 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: HealthCore evidence + clarifying tech asks

Kimberly / Jonas — quick internal note to capture the specific artifacts we'll need to include in the pack and a few clarifying asks from HealthCore's note: 

Required artifacts (initial pack):
- Current subprocessor list (purpose + whether they touch raw prompts/responses).
- Tenant config snapshot showing model_improvement=false and related flags (telemetry_enabled=false where applicable).
- Sample audit log extract (redacted timestamps/IDs) showing no training pipeline handoff for a sample interaction.
- Architecture diagram indicating KV cache behavior and retention windows.

Clarifying ops questions to confirm with Susan:
1) Retention window expectation — HealthCore is asking for "no-training evidence"; do they need explicit proof of deletion of telemetry after X days? If so, what X?
2) KMS residency — they mentioned onshore KMS. Are they expecting a BYOK HSM or is region-limited KMS acceptable?
3) Subprocessor scope — for any subprocessor that performs ML services, we must flag whether they have access to de-identified telemetry only.

Jonas — can you confirm whether we can produce the redacted audit log extract within the 72-hour timeline and whether the infrastructure team needs a formal JIRA request for any SFTP/export jobs? Also, we should confirm whether disabling telemetry has any impact on observability we rely on to meet SLAs (call it out in the pack).

I can draft the sample DPA clause language for "no-model-training" and "output ownership" to align with HealthCore legal once we confirm artifacts.

Thanks,
David
Privacy and Policy, Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Susan Liu <susan.liu@healthcore.com>, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: david.kim@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2028 14:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capture classification and non-training assurance — ops details and evidence cadence

Hi Susan / Kimberly — operations detail below to support the evidence pack. I'm attaching a one-page diagram shortly (ops-evidence-architecture-diagram.png) but the key points: 

- model_improvement flag: account-level boolean that prevents any customer interaction (prompts, files, session transcripts) from being routed to our model-improvement pipelines. The flag is versioned in our config store and we can provide a signed snapshot and API call history proving the setting for HealthCore's tenant.

- Audit logs: we can generate a redacted audit extract showing interaction processing stages. The extract will show that for interactions from your tenant the pipeline stops prior to the training queue and there is no handoff record. We will redact PII and provide explanation of each log field. Estimate: 48–72 hours to assemble and redact.

- KV cache / ephemeral state: short-lived KV caches are used to accelerate sessions but are not persisted to long-term storage when model_improvement=false. We'll document retention times (default 24 hours for ephemeral, configurable) and the architecture diagram will highlight cache boundaries.

- Subprocessors: current list attached; we will annotate which subprocessors ever touch raw prompts. For Hosted customers some analytics partners receive telemetry; for Dedicated/Private we can restrict to on-prem/onshore data-handling partners where required.

- KMS / residency: options are: (A) Redwood-managed KMS with region limitation, (B) customer-managed KMS (BYOK) with keys stored in HealthCore's region, or (C) dedicated on-prem HSM via Private deployment. We'll note tradeoffs in the evidence pack.

Operational caveat: fully disabling telemetry reduces our ability to produce per-request traces; if HealthCore wants extended SLA-level tracing while also blocking model improvement, we should document the minimal retained fields required for debugging and propose a retention window. We'll include suggested redaction patterns to minimize exposure.

Next steps: Kimberly — if you confirm, I'll produce the annotated subprocessor list and the redacted log extract; we'll aim to deliver the initial pack within 72 business hours after HealthCore returns the signed addendum/NDA.

Best,
Jonas
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

--
Attachments referenced: ops-evidence-architecture-diagram.png (diagram), subprocessor-inventory.csv (CSV stub)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Susan Liu <susan.liu@healthcore.com>
Cc: david.kim@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2028 21:45:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Capture classification and non-training assurance — confirm next steps

Susan — thanks, everyone. Confirming next steps and deliverables so we have a single source of truth: 

1) Redwood to deliver an initial evidence pack containing: annotated subprocessor list, config snapshot showing model_improvement=false, a redacted audit-log extract, and the ops architecture diagram. (Attachments included: healthcore-dpa-redline-v1.pdf; ops-evidence-architecture-diagram.png)
2) Estimated delivery: 72 business hours after signing the addendum/NDA (we can start production on receipt of a signed DocuSign link).
3) Kimberly will draft a short addendum paragraph for the DPA covering: no-model-training, customer ownership of inputs/outputs, and a clause on evidence delivery cadence. David will circulate that language for legal review.
4) Jonas will produce the log extract and annotate the subprocessor inventory; note about telemetry impact will be called out in the pack.

Please confirm and if acceptable I'll send a DocuSign for the addendum and trigger the evidence job.

Thanks — Kimberly
